petition to the British?

Sati was an inhuman practice

detailedSolution:

The Right to Information Act 2005 (Act No. 22/2005) is a law enacted by the
Parliament of India giving Indians access to government records. Under
the terms of the Act, any person may request information from a “public
authority” (a body of Government or instrumentality of State) which is
expected to reply expeditiously or within thirty days. The Act also requires
every public authority to computerize their records for wide dissemination
and to proactively publish certain categories of information so that the
citizens need minimum recourse to request for information formally. This
law was passed by Parliament on 15 June 2005 and came into force on 13
October 2005. Information disclosure in India was hitherto restricted by the
Official Secrets Act 1923 and various other special laws, which the new RTI
Act now overrides. The Act specifies that citizens have a right to:
 
• Request any information (as defined)
• Take copies of documents
• Inspect documents, works and records
• Take certified samples of materials of work
• Obtain information in the form of printouts, diskettes, floppies, tapes,
video cassettes or in any other electronic mode
Within how many days, a public authority is expected to reply under RTI?

20 days
41 days
10 days

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
For RTI Act 2005: 30-Day Response Timeline (Structure of Indian Society):
As verbatim specified in the passage, the public authority must reply 'expeditiously or within thirty days' of receiving the citizen's application.

Therefore, option (A) is the correct answer.

questionText:

passage:
The demographic advantage or ‘dividend’ to be derived from the age
structure of the population is due to the fact that India is (and will remain
for some time) one of the youngest countries in the world. A third of India’s
population was below 15 years of age in 2011. In 2020, the average Indian
was only 29 years old, compared with an average age of 37 in China and
the United States, 45 in Western Europe, and 48 in Japan. This implies a
large and growing labor force, which can deliver unexpected benefits in
terms of growth and prosperity.
 
When does Demographic Dividend takes place?

options.text:
When relatively smaller proportion of working-age people carry the burden
of providing for a relatively larger proportion of dependents.
When there is larger proportion of workers relative to non-workers.

When the proportion between working age people is equivalent to non-
working age people.
When the difference is zero between birth rate and death rate.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT principles for Structure of Indian Society (Conditions for Demographic Dividend):
When there is larger proportion of workers relative to non-workers.

Detailed Analysis:
As stated in the passage and NCERT, when the workforce (aged 15–64) expands rapidly relative to dependent children (0–14) and the elderly (65+), output per capita rises.

Therefore, option (C) is the correct answer.

topic: Social Reform Movements: Arya Samaj in Punjab
questionText:
Reading Comprehension Passage
 
Read the passage carefully and answer the questions that follows
 
New technologies speeded up various forms of communication. The
printing press, telegraph, and later the microphone, movement of people
and goods through steamship and railways helped quick movement of new
ideas. Within India, social reformers from Punjab and Bengal exchanged
ideas with reformers from Madras and Maharashtra. Keshav Chandra Sen
of Bengal visited Madras in 1864. Pandita Ramabai travelled to different
corners of the country. Some of them went to other countries. Christian
missionaries reached remote corners of present day Nagaland, Mizoram
and Meghalaya. Modern social organisations like the Brahmo Samaj in
Bengal and Arya Samaj in Punjab were set up. The All-India Muslim Ladies
Conference (Anjuman-E-Khawatn-E-Islam) was founded in 1914. Indian
reformers debated not just in public meetings but through public media
like newspapers and journals. Translations of writings of social reformers
from one Indian language to another took place. For instance, Vishnu
Shastri published a Marathi translation of Vidyasagar's book in Indu
Prakash in 1868.
Arya Samaj was set up in which state?

options.text: Punjab
Maharashtra
Bengal
Gujarat

According to NCERT principles for New Arenas of Social Change & Social Movements (Social Reform Movements: Arya Samaj in Punjab):
Punjab

Detailed Analysis:
The passage confirms: 'Modern social organisations like the Brahmo Samaj in Bengal and Arya Samaj in Punjab were set up.' In Punjab, the Arya Samaj spearheaded educational expansion through the Dayanand Anglo-Vedic (DAV) institutions.

Therefore, option (A) is the correct answer.

chapter: Social Inequality and Exclusion
questionText: Which of the following sociologically describes the notion of "minority"?

options.text: Aggressive unification of numerically smaller groups into bigger groups.
All those who are denied universal adult suffrage.

Relatively small disadvantaged group with a heightened sense of
solidarity.

Numerically small group of wealthy businessmen with a heightened
sense of solidarity.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT principles for Social Inequality and Exclusion (Sociological Definition of 'Minority'):
Relatively small disadvantaged group with a heightened sense of
solidarity.

Detailed Analysis:
Even if a group is numerically significant (or even a majority, like Black South Africans under Apartheid), they are sociologically a minority if they are systematically excluded from wealth, power, and prestige and possess heightened group consciousness.

Therefore, option (A) is the correct answer.

topic: Pierre Bourdieu: Three Forms of Capital
questionText:
Social resources can be divided into three forms of capital. Which of the
following is NOT among these?

options.text: Social capital
Economic capital
Natural capital
Cultural capital

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT principles for Social Inequality and Exclusion (Pierre Bourdieu: Three Forms of Capital):
Natural capital

Detailed Analysis:
According to Bourdieu:
1. Economic capital: Material resources, cash, and tangible assets.
2. Cultural capital: Educational credentials, linguistic skills, and cultural taste.
3. Social capital: Networks of mutual acquaintance and influential connections.
'Natural capital' is not a component of Bourdieu's framework.

Therefore, option (A) is the correct answer.

chapter: The Challenges of Unity in Diversity
topic: Implementation of the States Reorganisation Act: 1956
questionText:
Read the passage carefully and answer the questions based on the
passage:
 
The background to the SRC is as follows. In the 1920s, the Indian National
Congress was reconstituted on linguistic lines. Its provincial units now
followed the logic of language – one for Marathi speakers, another for
Oriya speakers, etc. At the same time, Gandhi and other leaders promised
their followers that when freedom came, the new nation would be based on
a new set of provinces based on the principle of language. However, when
India was finally freed in 1947, it was also divided. Now, when the
proponents of linguistic states asked for this promise to be redeemed, the
Congress hesitated. Partition was the consequence of intense attachment
to one’s faith; how many more partitions would that other intense loyalty,
language, lead to?
 
 
 
When was the Report of the States Reorganisation Commission (SRC)
implemented?
detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
For Implementation of the States Reorganisation Act: 1956 (The Challenges of Unity in Diversity):
The States Reorganisation Act 1956 reorganized state boundaries on linguistic grounds, creating 14 states and 6 union territories, which stabilized India's federal structure.

Therefore, option (B) is the correct answer.

chapter: Structure of Indian Society
questionText:
What is the purpose of the Pre-natal Diagnostic Techniques (Regulation
and Prevention of Misuse) Act?

options.text: To prevent misuse of technology for selective abortions.
To prevent abortion due to poverty and ignorance.
To prevent female infanticide.
To give incentives to families to raise girl child.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT principles for Structure of Indian Society (Pre-natal Diagnostic Techniques (PNDT) Act):
To prevent misuse of technology for selective abortions.

Detailed Analysis:
The Act prohibits sex selection before or after conception and bans prenatal diagnostic techniques from determining and disclosing the sex of a foetus, imposing severe penalties on violating clinics.

Therefore, option (A) is the correct answer.

chapter: Structure of Indian Society
questionText: What is "demographic dividend"?

options.text:
It happens when the birth rate is high but the death rate is low in the
population.

It happens when there is high migration of the population from rural to
urban areas.

It happens with an increase in the proportion of workers relative to non-
workers in the population.

It happens when both the birth rate and the death rate are low in the
population.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT principles for Structure of Indian Society (Concept of Demographic Dividend):
It happens with an increase in the proportion of workers relative to non-
workers in the population.

Detailed Analysis:
According to NCERT, India's changing age structure offers a temporary window of economic opportunity, as the productive working workforce outnumbers children and the elderly, lowering the national dependency ratio.

Therefore, option (D) is the correct answer.
